question: Have any of the IMERG Late Run's input satellites, instruments, datasets or data feeds, or their providers, faced funding cuts, operational disruptions, end-of-life decisions or termination announcements between January 2024 and November 2026, and how could that affect the Late Run?
searched_on: What is the status of the GPM Core Observatory (GMI, DPR): outages, end-of-life plans, Senior Review and budget treatment, and a successor?
What is the status of AMSR2 on GCOM-W1 and its successor AMSR3 on GOSAT-GW: end of life, data release and use in IMERG?
What has happened to SSMIS on DMSP and WSF-M MWI: data-sharing decisions, feed changes, outages, end of life, and how GPM handles them?
What has happened to MHS on NOAA-18/-19 and MetOp-B/-C, and to the MetOp-SG successors: decommissioning, failures and launches?
What has happened to ATMS on Suomi NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21: end of life, anomalies and successors?
What has happened to geostationary IR through NOAA CPC (merged 4-km IR) and its satellites: transitions, gaps and cuts tied to it?
What is the status, funding and recent change of PDIR-NOW / PERSIANN-CCS (CHRS) and the GPCC gauge analyses (DWD), and how do they reach the Late Run?
What has happened to the other inputs (GEOS FP motion vectors, GPROF/L1C, other sensors), and has NASA announced substitutes, pauses or version changes?
